chosen.premise: Magikarp can leap high, but its rare jumps never exceed seven feet—unless it has lived long enough to leap a mountain.
chosen.hook: Magikarp has a seven-foot jump limit... with one absurd exception.
chosen.visualIdea: Show a seven-foot height marker, then smash-cut to an aged Magikarp vaulting over a mountain.
chosen.note: A highly specific contradiction directly supported by two Pokédex entries: a usual seven-foot ceiling versus a mountain-leaping exception. The visual escalation is immediate and clear.

candidates.premise: Magikarp cannot swim against even slow currents, so rivers wash them into pools and deposit them there.
candidates.hook: Magikarp doesn't choose its pond—the river delivers it.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate Magikarp drifting down a river, collecting in a pool like fish being deposited by a conveyor belt.
candidates.note: Very concrete, unusually specific behavior with excellent animation potential. It is slightly less surprising to knowledgeable fans because Magikarp’s poor swimming is well known.

candidates.premise: The Pokédex calls Magikarp the world's weakest Pokémon, yet it survives in polluted water anywhere in the world.
candidates.hook: The world's weakest Pokémon may also be one of its toughest survivors.
candidates.visualIdea: Contrast a flopping Magikarp labeled “weakest” with increasingly murky water it calmly survives in.
candidates.note: Strongly supported and visually clear, but the weak-versus-tough-survivor contrast is a familiar Magikarp framing and less distinctive than the jump-limit contradiction.

candidates.premise: Magikarp was once stronger, but gradually weakened over time before evolving at level 20 into Gyarados.
candidates.hook: Magikarp's origin story is a Pokémon getting weaker before getting stronger.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a timeline draining Magikarp's strength, then trigger level 20 and transform it into Gyarados.
candidates.note: The weakening-before-evolving premise is compelling, but the research does not establish a direct causal timeline between ancient strength, gradual decline, and level-20 evolution. The transformation visual is also more conventional.

candidates.premise: Magikarp's reckless jumping makes it easy prey, but its abundance lets many Pokémon live longer by feeding on it.
candidates.hook: Magikarp's worst habit may be helping other Pokémon survive.
candidates.visualIdea: Follow a jumping Magikarp spotted by a predator, then widen out to countless Magikarp feeding entire ecosystems.
candidates.note: The predator-and-food-web contrast is supported, but “feeding entire ecosystems” overstates the evidence, which only says many Pokémon enjoy longer life spans thanks to Magikarp.
